value: The 2016 Expert Survey on Progress in AI, conducted by Grace et al. among machine learning researchers, investigated forecasts for High-Level Machine Intelligence (HLMI)—defined as machines outperforming humans at all tasks—and other AI developments. Key findings include a median 50% chance of HLMI by 2057, later than prior surveys, and significant methodological effects where question framing (e.g., asking about specific occupations vs. general HLMI) substantially influenced predicted timelines. The survey also highlighted expected progress in many narrow AI tasks within the next decade and revealed broad support among researchers for AI safety concerns, with a median 5% probability assigned to extremely negative long-term impacts (including human extinction) from advanced AI, and a desire for increased safety research.
